title: The Aitareya Upanishad, with Shankara's commentary
attributionNote: Anonymous. It is the fourth book of the Aitareya Aranyaka of the Rigveda and is named after its traditional teacher, Mahidasa Aitareya. The commentary beside the text is ascribed to Shankara.
description: In a few pages the Aitareya tells how the self first thought the worlds and the guardians of the worlds, and then entered in: the gods tried to eat and could not until he gave them the bodies they work through, and from the same self grew speech, sight, hearing, mind and breath and the food that sustains them. Its first verse, that all this was the self alone before creation, is the sentence of the Upanishad.
historicalContext: Placed fourth among the principal Upanishads and read with the Rigveda, it is cited in the Vedanta literature for its account of the self as the maker and the knower. Being short, it is one of the Upanishads chanted most often at the close of study.
availabilityNote: Complete: the three adhyayas of the GRETIL e-text, streamed at read time one khanda at a time, with the commentary ascribed to Shankara in a second pane.
